messages:
sophia: heads-up — i sketched a proposal for making the inflight prober more adaptive during model onboarding. goal: cut wasted bench runs and reduce false rejections when a model is close but noisy. PTAL.

mike: link?

sophia: https://tiny.fake/redwood/prober-adaptivity (sketch). tl;dr: instead of fixed probe windows (N trials, fixed latency/accuracy thresholds), we run a short adaptive stage that expands tests only if early signals are borderline.

anna: curious: what are the main signals you use to decide "borderline"?

sophia: good q. primary: variance on golden token log-prob, tail latency p95 vs p50, and token output divergence on a small golden set (BLEU-ish / embedding dist). if both variance and tail latency are within X, we skip full bench and mark as fast-path accept.

tariq: how do we avoid a model gaming the golden set? i.e., overfit to the tiny golden inputs and look fine but fail in larger evals.

sophia: we keep the golden set rotated per-run from a larger pool, and require consistency across two different golden slices before skipping heavy bench. also require KV-cache smoke to pass.

jess: does the proposal change any gating semantics? we still need hard rejects for non-interop binaries, right?

sophia: yes — hard rejects (ABI mismatch, missing tensors, obvious failure) stay unchanged. this is purely about reducing full-bench work for "borderline pass" models. soft decisions become two-stage: quick-scan -> conditional full-bench.

bot-bench: automation note: added metric hooks for `probe_variance` and `probe_tail_latency` to bench events. will emit `probe_adaptive_decision` tag.

mike: tradeoffs? sounds like fewer full benches but more complexity + more edgecases in the coordinator. any perf/regress risk?

sophia: main risks: 1) we accidentally accept models that later fail rare workloads (mitigation: sampled deferred full-bench within 24h), 2) coordinator bugs causing indeterminate states (mitigation: run feature as opt-in and soft-fail to full-bench on error).

anna: rollout plan? opt-in per-team? global flag?

sophia: propose: feature-flagged per-namespace. pilot with internal team (search) for 2 weeks. collect FAKE_METRIC: `deferred_failure_rate`. if <0.5% after 2w, widen to all onboardings for non-enterprise customers.

tariq: metrics to watch during pilot: deferred_failure_rate, proportion_full_bench_saved, median_onboard_latency, and post-onboard-invoice delta (cost).

sophia: yep — and we add an eval-sampling hook: 5% of fast-path acceptances get forced full-bench for extra safety.

jess: operational: add a single alert for `probe_adaptive_decision` spike and an oncall runbook to flip feature off quickly. also add a dashboard showing golden-slice overlap stats.

sophia: agreed. I'll update the RFC sketch with rollout steps, flag keys, and the coordinator pseudo-code. putting a short pseudo snippet here for the decision loop:

```
// pseudo
scan = run_short_probe(model, golden_slice1)
if scan.variance < V && scan.tail_p95 < L:
  if check_kv_smoke(model) and crosscheck(golden_slice2):
    tag = "fast-path-accept"
    maybe_defer_full_bench(5percent_sampling)
  else:
    enqueue_full_bench(model)
else:
  enqueue_full_bench(model)
```

mike: looks reasonable. two asks before pilot: 1) add explicit time budget (e.g. short_probe <= 30s), 2) define numeric thresholds or at least calibration run to derive V and L per model family.

sophia: yes to both. will run a calibration job against last 30 days of onboard data to propose thresholds per family. will aim for `short_probe <= 30s` and default `5%` sampling.

tariq: can we reuse existing bench telemetry infra for calibration? don't want to ship new ETL.

bot-bench: yes — calibration can reuse bench-history aggregates and the new `probe_variance` metric. will add a calibration job template.

anna: ok — i'm +1 for pilot once the calibration numbers are in and we have the dashboard + alert. please add a brief testing checklist (unit tests for decision logic, e2e pilot run, rollback smoke).

sophia: will do. thanks all — i'll post updated sketch + PR for the feature flag and coordinator changes tomorrow. :raised_hands:
